I have been composting stuff for years. First, I did the three-box composting for a while, where you fill one box, then turn it all over into a second one, and then again into a third one to finish. Then, to save space, I switched to composting in a wire-mesh circle for a while - this is less work, because the chicken-wire lets the compost 'breathe' better and you don't have to turn it over.

But then I started trying what I call 'composting in-situ'. Basically, dig a hole about the size of a flowerpot. Dump your kitchen-waste, rabbit poop, dead mice, chicken bones, fish heads, sour milk, whatever... cover it with some shredded paper, water it well and top off the hole with the soil you had dug out. And dig a hole next to it, so you can fill it next week. Then I plant whatever I need to plant in this. Directly, sometimes within a week or two of having buried it. Much less work because I don't have to fuck around with turning the pile, or worry about whether I have enough greens or browns to get to the right temperature. You have a lot of plant trimmings this week, well dig three holes instead of one. It uses next to no space, doesn't stink up anything, and so far I don't see a downside. When I started, I used to put a plywood board over the newly filled 'hole' because I was worried about raccoon-fags, but after a while I forgot to do that and nothing bad happened. It also seems to have improved the soil quality significantly more than top-dressing with compost, because the shit decomposes in the planting hole, with literally clumps of earthworms.

Long story short, this is the last year that I am going to fuck around with compost piles. Dig a hole, fill it halfway with organic waste, water it thoroughly, and close it off with soil. That's my plan from now on.
